newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Humana statement on Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Humana statement on Q4 earnings.

text.p: Humana Inc reported Q4 operating profits of $0.19 per share, compared to $0.30 the year earlier. First Call's Q4 analysts mean estimate was $0.21 per share. The company issued the following commentary with its fourth quarter earnings report. A table summarizing results ran separately.
Humana Announces Fourth Quarter And Year End Results

LOUISVILLE, Ky., Feb. 11 /PRNewswire/ -- Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) today reported fourth quarter earnings of $.19 per share, which excludes a previously announced charge of $.06 per share related to a planned work force reduction. The company reported $.30 per share for the same period in 1995.

Premium revenues for the fourth quarter grew 22 percent to $1.8 billion from $1.5 billion for the fourth quarter 1995. The increase was due to revenues earned under Humana's contract with the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Uniformed Services (CHAMPUS) as well as Medicare risk membership growth.
Medical membership at December 31, 1996 totaled a record 4.9 million members, compared to 3.8 million members at December 31, 1995, primarily due to the addition of CHAMPUS eligible members.

Medicare risk membership increased 17,100 members during the quarter. For 1996, Medicare risk membership grew 54,100 members or 17 percent, more than double the previous year's growth of 23,000 members or 8 percent.

Total commercial membership declined 31,600 members during the fourth quarter, primarily as a result of the company's planned exit from unprofitable markets and pricing of commercial products at rates designed to improve profitability. For the year, commercial membership declined 69,100 members. For both the quarter and year, membership losses from the exit of unprofitable markets and the proper pricing of commercial products were partially offset by increases in the small group (former EMPHESYS) platform.
In January, commercial membership declined 87,500 members, while membership in administrative services products increased approximately 67,000 members.

"Our plans to withdraw from certain markets and price business commensurate with the underlying risk are proceeding on schedule," said Gregory H. Wolf, Humana's president and chief operating officer. "Commercial membership will decrease an additional 115,000 members during the remainder of the first quarter, primarily as a result of the sale of our Washington, D.C. and Alabama operations. After these two sales are completed, commercial membership should begin to grow modestly."

Excluding special charges related to the work force reduction, fourth quarter net income was $32 million compared to $49 million reported in the same period a year ago. The decline in net income resulted from an increase in medical and administrative costs, offset partially by the profitability added by the growth in Medicare risk membership.

Humana's medical loss ratio for the fourth quarter was 82.8 percent compared to 81.5 percent in 1995. The higher ratio resulted from increased utilization of medical services in the areas of outpatient services and pharmacy costs.

The administrative cost ratio for the fourth quarter was 15.8 percent compared to 14.9 percent for the same period in 1995. The increase in the administrative cost ratio is the result of investment spending in such areas as customer service, information systems, marketing, and programs designed to increase Medicare risk membership.

"Our work to rebuild core processes began in earnest during the fourth quarter. Throughout 1997, we will invest heavily in medical management, information systems and customer service, areas critical to our long-term success," said Mr. Wolf.

During the fourth quarter, the company announced a special charge of approximately $15 million ($10 million, net of tax, or $.06 per share) related to the elimination of 700 to 900 positions during 1997. The work force reduction is a result of process improvement initiatives and will enable the company to redirect resources to its investment initiatives. Including the special charge, net income for the fourth quarter was $22 million, or $.13 per share.

For the year ended December 31, 1996, Humana's premium revenues increased 46 percent to a record $6.7 billion compared to $4.6 billion in 1995. Net income was $152 million or $.93 per share, compared to $190 million or $1.17 per share a year ago. The 1996 results exclude the charge for the work force reduction and the second quarter special charge of $200 million ($130 million, net of tax, or $.80 per share) for the restructuring of the company's Washington, D.C. health plan, provision for expected losses on insurance contracts, closing 13 service areas, and discontinuing unprofitable products in three markets. Including both of these special charges, net income for 1996 was $12 million or $.07 per share.

Humana Inc., headquartered in Louisville, Ky., is one of the nation's largest publicly-traded managed health care companies with 4.9 million medical members located primarily in 22 states. Humana offers coordinated health care through a variety of plans -- health maintenance organizations, preferred provider organizations, point-of-service plans and administrative services products -- to employer groups, government-sponsored plans and individuals.
